title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 1 — Pilot Variant 4

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. What is the required arrival time for the workshop?
tasks.audioText: New students will receive a workshop orientation on Monday at eight forty-five. Please wait at the marked reception point until the instructor collects the group. The briefing will explain the workshop layout, emergency exits and local reporting arrangements. Students must follow the instructor's directions and must not enter restricted areas without permission.

tasks.prompt: During a workshop induction, students learned where to find the first-aid point and how to report a damaged tool. The instructor explained that a warning label must remain visible and that equipment should not be used if its condition is uncertain. Students were also shown the designated walkways and reminded to ask before entering a restricted work area. Reading 1. What should students do if a tool is damaged?
options: Report it to the appropriate person

tasks.prompt: Why must warning labels remain visible?
options: So that users can see the relevant warning

tasks.prompt: Students must ___ the instructor's directions during the induction.
Choose TWO items normally covered in a workshop induction.
A formal introduction that explains local rules and safety arrangements is an ___.
You notice a damaged tool in the workshop. What should you say?
options: I will keep using it until it stops working.
I have noticed a damaged tool. Who should I report it to?
I will hide it so nobody sees it.
It is probably safe, so there is no need to tell anyone.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of workshop orientation in a logical order.
options: Identify reporting points and emergency exits
Ask the instructor about any unclear instruction
Learn the workshop layout and local rules
correctOrder: Learn the workshop layout and local rules
Identify reporting points and emergency exits
Ask the instructor about any unclear instruction

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words describing why workshop induction is important. Include two examples of information students should learn.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: task completion and relevant content (0–2); clear organisation and logical linking (0–2); grammar and sentence structure (0–2); accurate technical vocabulary, spelling and punctuation (0–2). Minor errors are acceptable if meaning remains clear.
